clue.text: Patience when abused may succeed in circling the world

indicators.note: circling says the word for succeeding goes round the word for the world

parts.note: to succeed is to win
the world we live on is the Earth

explanation.surface: A mild proverb: mistreated patience may still triumph and travel the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sentence that the answer completes: patience, when abused, may run out. 'in' just links the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience that is tried too often becomes exhausted, the idiom being that it frays like overused cloth.

clue.text: Bird that sounds piercing

indicators.note: sounds says we take how a word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a skewer is a spike for piercing meat

explanation.surface: A bird whose call is shrill and sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piercing' looks like an adjective for a sound, but it stands for SKEWER, which said in a non-rhotic accent matches the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A skua is a large predatory seabird of the gull family.

clue.text: Ways to secure love that inspires pity

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the noun: the quality that inspires pity

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the word for ways holds the letter for love

parts.note: ways are paths
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Methods of keeping affection that end up making people feel sorry for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in art or life that moves an audience to sorrow and compassion.

clue.text: Look up to speaker's lazy eyes

indicators.note: speaker's says the words are as spoken aloud, not as written

parts.note: lazy eyes are idle eyes

explanation.surface: Gazing up admiringly at a talker with drooping eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lazy eyes' sounds like a medical condition; spoken, IDLE EYES runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone as a hero is to look up to them, treating them as an idol.

clue.text: A British girl put on pounds: unusual?

parts.note: Norma is a girl's name
L, from the Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A British woman gaining weight, and whether that is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on pounds' reads as weight gain, but it only places NORMA on L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abnormal departs from the norm, which is what unusual means.

clue.text: Don't purify murky depth

indicators.note: murky means muddied and unclear, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction not to clean water whose murk hides its depth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'murky' rearranges the letters of DONT PURIFY.
explanation.definitionFit: Profundity is depth of thought or feeling, from the Latin for deep.

clue.text: Before St David's Day the Guardian declares a republic

indicators.note: Before says the newspaper's word comes ahead of the date

parts.note: a newspaper speaks of itself with the editorial 'we'
St David's Day, Wales's national day, is 1 March, written I MAR

explanation.surface: A newspaper proclaiming a new republic on the eve of a Welsh saint's day.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numeral I gives the 1 in 1 March, abbreviated MAR. 'declares' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weimar Republic was Germany's democratic state between 1919 and 1933.

clue.text: Ordinary seaman's two sets of cards

parts.note: the first set of cards is a deck, a full pack
the second set of cards is a hand, the cards dealt to one player

explanation.surface: A sailor carrying a couple of packs of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is a crew member doing manual work on deck, the lowest seagoing rank.

clue.text: Lighter to bump into

definitions.meaning: a lighter is a flat-bottomed boat for moving cargo
to collide clumsily with someone, as in to shove past

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like a cigarette lighter or a comparison of weight; here it is a cargo boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge is a flat-bottomed cargo boat like a lighter, and to barge into someone is to knock into them.

clue.text: Extent of some software amazing

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: How far some impressive computer program reaches.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is the extent of a surface or a range of activity.

clue.text: Welcome s-success, to be admitted here

parts.note: hallo is a greeting of welcome
success is fame, and the stammered hyphen form tells us to repeat its first letter

explanation.surface: A stuttering greeting to someone whose success earns them entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 's-success' is copied onto the synonym: FAME stammered becomes F-FAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall of fame is a roll of honour into which famous achievers are inducted.

clue.text: Runs after luggage round hotel

indicators.note: round says the word for luggage goes round the letter for hotel

parts.note: suitcases are luggage
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone chasing after their bags left near a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase someone is to pursue, to go running after them.

clue.text: Petty criminal who tells on his accomplices?

definitions.text: Petty criminal who tells on his accomplices?

parts.words: Petty criminal who tells on his accomplices?
parts.note: a 'sneak' is a telltale, so a thief who sneaks on his mates fits the joke

explanation.walkthrough: The real term means a stealthy thief who slips in unseen; the clue pretends 'sneak' means an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak thief steals without breaking in or using violence, a small-time burglar.

clue.text: Marines trained for a year in academy

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are drilled into a new formation

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Marines spending a year of training at a military academy.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college, especially one training priests, so an academy.

clue.text: Serious tennis played by European

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are put through their paces into another order

explanation.surface: A grave game of tennis played by a European.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means earnest and deeply felt, near in sense to serious.

clue.text: Only for men: old woman has time still

parts.note: a stag party or night is for men only
nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: A men-only event where a grandmother still turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' sits at the end looking like an adverb; it is the adjective, as in still water.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is still, not flowing.

clue.text: Gangster catcalls heard in capital

indicators.note: heard says we take the spoken form of the words

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster and catcalls are jeers

explanation.surface: A mobster's jeering heard in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: AL (Capone) plus JEERS, said aloud, gives the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Algiers is the capital city of Algeria.

clue.text: Call about oven for cooking

indicators.note: about says the word for calling goes round the word for oven

parts.note: to ring is to call by phone
an oast is a kiln, an oven for drying hops

explanation.surface: Phoning about an oven so you can cook.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is the kiln with a cowled roof used in Kent to dry hops.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasting is a way of cooking food in an oven with dry heat.

clue.text: Dog we held up in entrance

indicators.note: in says the reversed pair goes inside the word for the dog

parts.note: a bitch is a female dog

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up says the word is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A dog stopping us at a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a doorway; it is the verb to enchant, stressed on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewitch is to cast a spell over, to enchant or entrance someone.

clue.text: Competition one may have in the bag

definitions.text: Competition one may have in the bag

parts.words: Competition one may have in the bag
parts.note: 'in the bag' means certain to win, but here the competitors literally stand in sacks

explanation.definitionFit: A sack race is a children's race in which runners hop along with their legs inside sacks.

clue.text: Stop thief!

parts.note: the shout raised after a fleeing thief is a call to halt and detain him

explanation.definitionFit: To arrest is to stop and seize someone, exactly what the cry demands be done to the thief.

clue.text: Holiday emergency!

definitions.meaning: the distress call used by ships and aircraft in an emergency

explanation.definitionFit: May Day is a spring holiday, and Mayday, from the French m'aidez, is the radio call for help.

clue.text: Mule is chewing cereal

indicators.note: chewing mashes the letters up into a new arrangement

explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit.

clue.text: Such a gripping tale we hear

definitions.text: Such a gripping tale we hear

parts.words: Such a gripping tale we hear
parts.note: a monkey's grasping tail has this name, and tail sounds like tale

explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping tale' reads as an exciting story; heard as 'tail', it is a monkey's tail that can grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehensile describes an organ able to grasp, as a monkey's tail or an elephant's trunk can.

clue.text: Old British settler needed for 20?

definitions.meaning: the ... were a Germanic people who settled in Kent in the fifth century
the coarse fibre that sacks are woven from, referring to the race at 20

explanation.definitionFit: Jutes settled early England, and jute is the fibre sacking is made from.

clue.text: Panel put into a box

parts.note: in court, the twelve people chosen to try a case sit in an enclosure called a box

explanation.definitionFit: A jury is a panel of citizens sworn to give a verdict, seated in the jury box.

clue.text: Rear small bird

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' looks like a verb, to bring up a chick; it is the noun, the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear part of a ship.

clue.text: 150 of the Romans stand for disinfectant

definitions.text: 150 of the Romans stand for disinfectant

parts.words: 150 of the Romans stand for disinfectant
parts.note: CL, Roman numerals for 150, is also the chemical symbol of the element used to disinfect pools

explanation.walkthrough: The Roman numerals for 150 are CL, which is also the chemical symbol for this element.
explanation.definitionFit: Chlorine is the gas added to water supplies and swimming pools to kill germs.
